chapter_title: Chapitre 3 -Impacts of Climate Change on the Agricultural Sector
summary: This chapter discusses the impacts of climate change on the agricultural sector, focusing on arable and livestock sectors and hydrology. It highlights both positive and negative impacts, emphasizing the need for adaptation strategies. It also presents specific examples from Korea, China, and India. The conceptual approach is to view agriculture as a climate-dependent bio-industry that is vulnerable to shifts in temperature, precipitation, and sunlight.
key_climate_change_impacts_on_agricultur: Changes in flowering and harvesting seasons
Shift of areas suitable for cultivation
Changes in livestock production (fertilization, breeding, pasture production)
Alterations in hydrology (underground water level, river flow, water quality)
Changes in agricultural productivity, farm household revenues, and asset values
Reduced crop quantity and quality due to temperature rise
Increased soil erosion due to increased rainfall
Worsening of freezing injury in early spring

specific_impacts_on_attributes.impact_description: Increased average temperatures leading to changes in crop suitability, flowering seasons, and overall agricultural production. Can cause heat stress, reduced crop quality, and shifts in suitable cultivation areas.

Altered rainfall patterns, including increased or decreased precipitation, affecting water availability for irrigation, increasing soil erosion, and leading to floods or droughts. Changes can affect river flow and water quality.

Increased atmospheric CO2 concentration which can lead to fertilization effects, potentially increasing crop productivity at low levels of temperature rise, but also leading to other negative consequences.
Shifting agricultural climate zones due to temperature rise.

vulnerable_crops_or_regions: Apples, peaches, grapes, and soybeans (affected by brown grasshoppers)
Hot-temperature fruits and vegetables (watermelons, peppers, tomatoes)
Wheat, rice, and corn in China
Forage in drought or semi-drought areas in China
mitigation_recommendations_for_agricultu: Enhanced agricultural production management methods (specifically for China)

Farmland price rise due to 1 mm precipitation increase
Drop in Chinese agricultural productivity by 2030
Decrease in yield of three major crops in China in the late 21st century
Loss of gross agricultural production in China due to blights and pests
Potential drop in total grain production due to climate change (2030-2050)
Summer monsoon contribution to annual rainfall
